new.title: Stand on Place Stanislas, Nancy's golden square
new.desc: Designed by Emmanuel Héré for Duke Stanislas Leszczynski and built from 1752 to 1756, the square links Nancy's old and new towns. With the Place de la Carrière and Place d'Alliance it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1983. Its gilded gates by Jean Lamour frame the Hôtel de Ville and the Opéra.
new.tip: Come at dusk when the gilding is lit, or during the Saint-Nicolas festivities for the light show. It was pedestrianised in 2005 and is free to enter.
new.q: Place Stanislas, Nancy

new.title: Walk the plane-lined Place de la Carrière
new.desc: A 16th-century jousting ground remodelled in the 18th century, this long tree-shaded promenade runs from the Arc Héré to the Palais du Gouvernement. A curved hémicycle decorated with 22 busts of antique figures closes the far end.
new.tip: Walk from the Arc Héré on Place Stanislas to the Palais du Gouvernement; the Pépinière park lies just behind. Free and best in the morning light.
new.q: Place de la Carrière, Nancy

new.title: See the ducal tombs in the Cordeliers church
new.desc: Beside the Palais des Ducs de Lorraine, the Église des Cordeliers became the dynastic necropolis of the dukes at the wish of René II. The Italian Baroque ducal chapel (1609-1612) has a trompe-l'oeil dome, and the church holds Ligier Richier's 1547 tomb of Philippe de Gueldre.
new.tip: The Musée lorrain next door is closed for renovation, but the church stays open to visitors free of charge. Check hours on the museum site.
new.q: Église des Cordeliers, 66 Grande Rue, Nancy

new.title: Visit Villa Majorelle, an Art Nouveau house
new.desc: Cabinetmaker Louis Majorelle commissioned this house from the young architect Henri Sauvage, built 1901-1902 under the supervision of Lucien Weissenburger. Also called Villa Jika after Majorelle's wife Jeanne Kretz, it has belonged to the City of Nancy since 2003 and reopened in February 2020 after restoration.
new.tip: Visits run through the Musée de l'École de Nancy and need advance booking; check the museum site for the current timetable.
new.q: Villa Majorelle, 1 rue Louis Majorelle, Nancy

new.title: Step into the Musée de l'École de Nancy
new.desc: Set in the former home of patron Eugène Corbin in a one-hectare park, the museum has shown Art Nouveau since 1964. It holds Gallé glass, the Daum cactus lamp, Majorelle bedroom furniture and works by Victor Prouvé from the 1901 École de Nancy alliance.
new.tip: Combine it with a stroll through Parc Sainte-Marie next door. Allow about 90 minutes.
new.q: Musée de l'École de Nancy, 36-38 rue du Sergent Blandan, Nancy

new.title: Admire the Daum glass at the Beaux-Arts museum
new.desc: On Place Stanislas, the Musée des Beaux-Arts keeps its Daum glassware collection in a dramatic basement display; the first piece, a 1904 floor lamp, entered in 1905. The collection documents the glassmaking tradition of Nancy alongside the museum's paintings.
new.tip: Visit on a rainy afternoon and look for the Daum basement gallery. Check the museum's site for hours and the free first-Sunday offers.
new.q: Musée des Beaux-Arts, 3 place Stanislas, Nancy

new.title: Pass under the medieval Porte de la Craffe
new.desc: The last remnant of Nancy's medieval fortifications and the oldest monument in the city centre, dating from about 1463. The dukes of Lorraine made their formal entrance through it, and it stands at the top of the Grande Rue.
new.tip: Start your Grande Rue walk here and head down towards the Palais ducal. It is free to see from outside.
new.q: Porte de la Craffe, 108 Grande Rue, Nancy

new.title: Gaze up at the Basilique Saint-Épvre
new.desc: This neo-Gothic basilica of Euville stone was designed by Prosper Morey and built from 1864 to about 1871. Its stained glass came from Austrian and Metz workshops and its bells were cast in Budapest.
new.tip: The spire is visible from the Pépinière park. There are no fixed visiting hours, so check for open times.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Épvre, Place Saint-Épvre, Nancy

new.title: Visit Nancy's baroque cathedral
new.desc: Begun in 1703 under Duke Léopold and continued under Stanislas, the Cathédrale Notre-Dame-de-l'Annonciation became a cathedral in 1777 when the bishopric moved from Toul. It mixes Baroque and neoclassical elements under a frescoed dome and has been a historic monument since 1906.
new.tip: It is an active parish, so avoid Mass times for a quiet visit. Entry is free.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame-de-l'Annonciation, Place Monseigneur Ruch, Nancy

new.title: Seek out Stanislas's tomb at Bonsecours
new.desc: King Stanislas had the Église Notre-Dame-de-Bonsecours built to plans by Héré between 1738 and 1741 on the site of a chapel raised by René II. It holds the tombs of Stanislas and his wife Catherine Opalinska, and has been a historic monument since 1906.
new.tip: Take a bus out along avenue de Strasbourg; check visiting times on the Nancy tourism site.
new.q: Église Notre-Dame-de-Bonsecours, Place Général Castelnau, Nancy

new.title: Meet the fish at the Muséum-Aquarium
new.desc: A natural history museum and aquarium under one Art Deco roof at 34 rue Sainte-Catherine. Tropical and temperate fish fill the tanks, and the zoology collection holds some 600 specimens of naturalised animals.
new.tip: Entry is free on the first Sunday of the month. Opening times vary, so check before going.
new.q: Muséum-Aquarium de Nancy, 34 rue Sainte-Catherine, Nancy

new.title: Tour the Opéra national de Lorraine
new.desc: The opera house stands on Place Stanislas and is open for guided visits that cover the peristyle, the Italian-style auditorium and the grand foyer in about an hour. It is the home of the Opéra national de Lorraine.
new.tip: Guided visits are booked online or at the box office, which is open Monday to Friday afternoons; check current dates first.
new.q: Opéra national de Lorraine, 1 rue Sainte-Catherine, Nancy

new.title: Wander the Jardin botanique Jean-Marie Pelt
new.desc: The botanical garden of Villers-lès-Nancy, renamed after biologist Jean-Marie Pelt in 2016, has thematic collections, an alpine garden of over 1,200 species and tropical greenhouses. It also keeps a herbarium of more than 300,000 sheets.
new.tip: Tram or bus 3, 17 or 30 to Villers Campus Sciences. The tropical greenhouses charge a separate fee.
new.q: Jardin botanique Jean-Marie Pelt, 100 rue du Jardin Botanique, Villers-lès-Nancy

new.title: Dine at the Art Nouveau Brasserie L'Excelsior
new.desc: Opened in 1911 near the station, this brasserie has furniture and chandeliers by Louis Majorelle and ten stained-glass windows by Jacques Gruber, plus an Art Deco extension with a Jean Prouvé banister. The main hall is a listed monument.
new.tip: Order a classic brasserie dish such as choucroute or a seafood platter. Book for evenings.
new.q: Brasserie L'Excelsior, 50 rue Henri Poincaré, Nancy

new.title: Taste a Nancy macaron at Sœurs Macarons
new.desc: The Maison des Sœurs Macarons on rue Gambetta sells the almond macaron of Nancy, together with chocolates and fruit jellies. The shop holds the Entreprise du Patrimoine Vivant label, though sources disagree on its founding year.
new.tip: Buy a box of plain macarons, the original recipe. Closed Sundays and Monday afternoons per a 2024 listing, so check hours.
new.q: Maison des Sœurs Macarons, 21 rue Gambetta, Nancy

new.title: Buy bergamotes de Nancy at Lefèvre-Lemoine
new.desc: The Au Duché de Lorraine shop of the Lefèvre-Lemoine family, in business since 1840, sells the protected bergamote sweet: a hard, amber, square candy of sugar, glucose and bergamot essence. Its listed Lorraine shop furniture has been protected since 2022.
new.tip: Pair the bergamotes with a visit to the Excelsior across the street. Closed Sunday afternoons per an older listing.
new.q: Au Duché de Lorraine Lefèvre-Lemoine, 47 rue Henri Poincaré, Nancy

new.title: Eat quiche lorraine at Les Frères Marchand
new.desc: A cheese-focused brasserie on the Grande Rue facing the Palais ducal, serving quiche lorraine, râpés (grated potato) and andouillette with Gros Lorrain cheese. Gault&Millau lists it at roughly 19 to 33 euros per person.
new.tip: Portions are generous and it gets busy, so book. The same family runs a cheese and charcuterie stall in the Marché Central.
new.q: Les Frères Marchand, Grande Rue, Nancy

new.title: Have a coffee at Grand Café Foy on the square
new.desc: Housed in what is called the oldest building on Place Stanislas, this historic brasserie at number 1 is named after General Maximilien Sébastien Foy. Its menu includes a quiche lorraine au lard paysan.
new.tip: Take a terrace table on the square for a coffee or the quiche; open long hours daily per listings.
new.q: Grand Café Foy, 1 place Stanislas, Nancy

new.title: Stroll the Parc de la Pépinière
new.desc: Created by Stanislas Leszczynski as a royal tree nursery from 1765 and opened to the public in the 19th century, the park covers about 21 hectares. Nancy residents call it la Pep'. It has been a site inscrit since 1947.
new.tip: Free and open all day; it is the hub of the Pépinière en Fête concerts during Nancy Jazz Pulsations.
new.q: Parc de la Pépinière, Nancy

new.title: Follow the Art Nouveau trail on Rue Félix Faure
new.desc: Rue Félix Faure is a rare coherent Art Nouveau street, with houses built 1900-1910 largely by architect César Pain. The tourism office's Art Nouveau route passes it on the way to Maison Lejeune and Parc Sainte-Marie.
new.tip: Pick up the free Art Nouveau trail leaflet from the tourist office; a cycling version of about 13 km also exists.
new.q: Rue Félix Faure, Nancy

new.title: Relax in the Parc Sainte-Marie
new.desc: A Jardin Remarquable of about 7.5 hectares, laid out on land the Jesuits settled in 1620 and made a private pleasure garden in 1808. Square plots are bordered by limes and hornbeams, a short walk from the École de Nancy museum.
new.tip: Free to enter; opens early in the morning. It links well with a run to the Pépinière park.
new.q: Parc Sainte-Marie, Nancy

new.title: Join the Saint-Nicolas festivities and grand parade
new.desc: Nancy's Saint-Nicolas festivities run from late November to early January, with a grand parade, video-mapping and fireworks on Place Stanislas, plus festive villages and markets. The 2026 parade is on Saturday 5 December.
new.tip: Free entry. Check saint-nicolas.nancy.fr for the exact programme and arrive early for the parade.
new.q: Place Stanislas, Nancy

new.title: Catch a concert at Nancy Jazz Pulsations
new.desc: A festival held every October with hundreds of concerts across the city, centred on the Chapiteau de la Pépinière. The free Pépinière en Fête programme runs in the park.
new.tip: Check nancyjazzpulsations.com for dates; 2026 is about 7 to 17 October. Tent concerts are ticketed.
new.q: Parc de la Pépinière, Nancy

new.title: Browse the Marché Central for Lorraine produce
new.desc: A 19th-century U-shaped covered market between Place Charles III and rue Saint-Dizier with around 65 traders. Look for charcuterie, tourtes (munster, pâté lorrain, rissoles) and cheeses from Les Frères Marchand.
new.tip: Go in the morning; it is an easy walk from Place Stanislas. The city is retendering its management, so check hours.
new.q: Marché Central, Place Henri Mengin, Nancy

new.title: Soak in the thermal pools at Nancy Thermal
new.desc: The 1913 spa beside Parc Sainte-Marie reopened in spring 2023 after renovation, with a thermal spa, an aquatic and sports centre and a hotel residence. The wellness area has hot thermal pools, saunas and hammams.
new.tip: Book a two-hour wellness entry online; prices in listings were around 20 euros, so check the current rate.
new.q: Nancy Thermal, 41-43 Esplanade Jacques Baudot, Nancy

new.title: Tour the Château de Lunéville, the Lorraine Versailles
new.desc: Rebuilt by Duke Léopold from 1703 with designs by Germain Boffrand, a pupil of Hardouin-Mansart, the château earned the nickname of the Versailles of Lorraine. Stanislas later lived and embellished it, and it is now a departmental museum and heritage site.
new.tip: The Parc des Bosquets behind it reopened largely to the public in June 2024; check the château site for closures.
new.q: Château de Lunéville, Lunéville

new.title: Explore Toul cathedral and its Gothic cloister
new.desc: The Cathédrale Saint-Étienne has stood since the 13th century with a Flamboyant west front, and has been a historic monument since 1840. Its cloister, about 54 by 42 metres, is one of the largest Gothic cloisters in France and shows early Renaissance decoration.
new.tip: The cloister is freely open in daytime. Check cathedral hours before going.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Étienne, Place Charles de Gaulle, Toul

new.title: See crystal at the Musée du cristal in Baccarat
new.desc: The museum is housed in the château built from 1764 on the grounds of the Baccarat crystal works and reopened in 2015. It presents about 1,100 objects and the manufacturing technique across four rooms.
new.tip: The factory's older Chapelle Sainte-Anne (1773) stands nearby. Check hours and entry price on the museum's site.
new.q: Musée Baccarat, 2 rue des Cristalleries, Baccarat

new.title: Marvel at the basilica of Saint-Nicolas-de-Port
new.desc: Built between 1481 and 1545 under René II in Flamboyant Gothic style, the basilica is a major pilgrimage church of St Nicholas. Its organ, built in 1848 by Joseph Cuvillier, has a case listed as a historic monument.
new.tip: It is a short train or bus ride from Nancy. Free entry; the Musée français de la Brasserie is in the same town.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Nicolas, Saint-Nicolas-de-Port

new.title: Visit the Abbaye des Prémontrés at Pont-à-Mousson
new.desc: This Premonstratensian abbey beside the Moselle was built between 1705 and 1735 and made a cultural centre in 1964. It hosts exhibitions, concerts and workshops, and associations are restoring its church choir.
new.tip: Check abbaye-premontres.com for exhibitions and opening hours; it is on the Voie Bleue cycle route.
new.q: Abbaye des Prémontrés, 9 rue Saint-Martin, Pont-à-Mousson

new.title: Climb to the ruins of Prény castle
new.desc: The last fortress of the dukes of Lorraine facing the bishops of Metz, rebuilt after 1207 and covering nearly three hectares. Parts were destroyed in the fighting of September to November 1918, and the ruins have been classified since 1862.
new.tip: Hiking loops of about 12.7 km start from the village in the Lorraine regional park. Wear sturdy shoes.
new.q: Château de Prény, Prény

new.title: Walk the Vauban ramparts of Longwy-Haut
new.desc: Vauban designed the enclosure of the upper town between 1679 and 1684, and the Porte de France dates from 1683. The fortifications form part of UNESCO's Fortifications of Vauban listing of 2008, and the site is a freely accessible park.
new.tip: Also visit the nearby municipal museum of enamels and faience by the Porte de France; listings show hours but verify them first.
new.q: Porte de France, Longwy-Haut, Longwy

new.title: Discover popular prints at the Musée de l'Image in Épinal
new.desc: The museum opened in 2003 on the Moselle and holds over 110,000 images, one of the major collections of popular French and foreign prints from the 17th century to today. It belongs to the Cité de l'Image, beside the Pellerin printworks founded in 1796.
new.tip: A joint ticket covers the museum and the Imagerie d'Épinal printing workshop next door. Check opening hours.
new.q: Musée de l'Image, 42 quai de Dogneville, Épinal

new.title: Visit Joan of Arc's birthplace at Domrémy
new.desc: The département bought Joan's family home in 1818 and visitors see four rooms, including the birth room, next to the parish church. A visitor centre behind it covers her childhood, her life and her afterlife as a myth. About 22,000 people visit each year.
new.tip: Domrémy is about 47 km from Nancy. Check maisonjeannedarc.vosges.fr for hours and tickets.
new.q: Maison natale de Jeanne d'Arc, 2 rue de la Basilique, Domrémy-la-Pucelle

new.title: Visit the Basilique du Bois-Chenu above Domrémy
new.desc: The basilica of Sainte-Jeanne-d'Arc stands on a wooded slope about 1.5 km south of Domrémy, where Joan is traditionally said to have heard her voices. Work started in 1881 to plans by Paul Sédille, and mosaics and paintings tell her story.
new.tip: Free admission; opening hours are given as about 8:00-19:00 from April to mid-October and 9:00-17:00 otherwise.
new.q: Basilique du Bois-Chenu, Domrémy-la-Pucelle

new.title: See the Roman amphitheatre and mosaic at Grand
new.desc: The amphitheatre of Grand is 148 metres along its long axis, among the ten largest in the Roman world, and may have held 16,000 to 20,000 people. The site also keeps a basilica mosaic of about 232 square metres, uncovered in 1883.
new.tip: The site is run by the Vosges département as Grand la Gallo-Romaine; see grandlagalloromaine.vosges.fr for opening times.
new.q: Amphithéâtre gallo-romain, Grand

new.title: Learn violin making at Mirecourt's lutherie museum
new.desc: The Musée de la Lutherie et de l'Archèterie françaises in Mirecourt, a Musée de France since 2002, holds 321 instruments and bows reflecting three centuries of the town's craft. In July and August a young apprentice luthier works in a visitable workshop.
new.tip: Hours in one listing are Tuesday to Saturday with a midday break; check musee-mirecourt.fr before you go.
new.q: Musée de la Lutherie et de l'Archèterie françaises, Cours Stanislas, Mirecourt

new.title: Tour the Manufacture Royale at Bains-les-Bains
new.desc: Founded in the 18th century, this tinplate works from 1733 is described as the oldest industrial site in Lorraine. It has a chapel, workers' housing, a park with ice house and an exhibition on tinplate; feminist pioneer Julie-Victoire Daubié was born there.
new.tip: Guided visits in 2025 ran on set Fridays from March to October at about 6 to 7 euros; confirm the current schedule.
new.q: Manufacture Royale, Bains-les-Bains, La Vôge-les-Bains

new.title: Count the windows at Château de Haroué
new.desc: Germain Boffrand designed the château for Marc de Beauvau-Craon, built about 1720 to 1732. Its plan counts the year: 365 windows, 52 chimneys, 12 towers and 4 bridges. It has been open to the public through the Centre des monuments nationaux since 2021.
new.tip: It is south of Nancy; check the CMN site for opening times and tickets.
new.q: Château de Haroué, Haroué

new.title: Walk the cloister of Saint-Dié cathedral
new.desc: The cathedral, the Romanesque church of Notre-Dame-de-Galilée and the Gothic cloister joining them form one listed ensemble. Galilée holds a Virgin and Child of about 1320 among the best-known Lorraine madonnas, and the cathedral dates from the diocese of 1777.
new.tip: Le Corbusier's Usine Duval nearby is private and not open to visits. Check cathedral hours locally.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Dié, Place du Général de Gaulle, Saint-Dié-des-Vosges

new.title: Taste Gris de Toul at Maison Lelièvre
new.desc: Founded at Lucey in 1971 and run by brothers Vincent and David Lelièvre, this domaine offers tasting and cellar visits for Côtes de Toul and Mirabelle de Lorraine. Its Gris de Toul rosé has cherry notes and a fresh, slightly bitter finish.
new.tip: Try the Gris de Toul with quiche lorraine or charcuterie, as the appellation suggests. Call ahead for tasting hours.
new.q: Maison Lelièvre, 1 rue de la Gare, Lucey

new.title: Lunch at the Art Deco Grande Brasserie du Commerce
new.desc: A town-centre brasserie dating from 1895 with wall tiles and a bistro atmosphere, serving seasonal cooking such as foie gras with saffron and tête de veau. À la carte prices are around 35 euros.
new.tip: Closed Sundays and Mondays per listings; the shaded terrace is pleasant in summer.
new.q: Grande Brasserie du Commerce, 10 place de la République, Toul

new.title: Taste mirabelle eaux-de-vie at Maison de la Mirabelle
new.desc: The Grallet-Dupic family distillery at Rozelieures runs a visit with tasting of three mirabelle eaux-de-vie distilled on site, and a shop selling its Rozelieures whisky range. It lies about 25 minutes from Lunéville.
new.tip: Visit prices in listings range from 6.50 euros to a 65 euro tasting package, so confirm before booking. Adults only for the spirit tasting.
new.q: Maison de la Mirabelle, 16 rue du Capitaine Durand, Rozelieures

new.title: Eat blueberry tart at J-E Schmitt in Gérardmer
new.desc: The chocolatier-pâtissier J-E Schmitt makes Vosges chocolates with mirabelle or bilberry and the house Granit des Vosges. A reviewer singles out its blueberry tart and praline macaron-style cake.
new.tip: Hours in a directory listing were 8:00-12:15 and 14:00-19:00, closed Mondays, so check before going.
new.q: Chocolatier Pâtissier Schmitt, 15 rue François Mitterrand, Gérardmer

new.title: Eat a farm meal at Ferme Auberge de la Mexel
new.desc: A farm-inn above Gérardmer serving the Hautes-Vosges repas marcaire: dishes noted include munster-stuffed potatoes, tourte, smoked pork and tofailles, a stewed potato with onion and bacon.
new.tip: Phone ahead for tables and current opening dates; the menu details in the source date from 2013.
new.q: Ferme Auberge de la Mexel, 66 chemin de la Mexel, Gérardmer

new.title: Order tourte at the Auberge du Pied du Hohneck
new.desc: A mountain inn on the Route des Crêtes at La Bresse, serving the Hautes-Vosges marcaire menu of meat tourte, smoked pork and munster. The La Bresse inn guide describes the tourte as a meat pie in puff pastry.
new.tip: Seasonal and weather-dependent on the Route des Crêtes, so call ahead.
new.q: Auberge du Pied du Hohneck, 1 route des Crêtes, La Bresse

new.title: Taste Vosges bonbons at the Confiserie Géromoise
new.desc: A certified organic sweet maker making bonbons des Vosges in mirabelle, honey or eucalyptus with essential oils and Hautes-Vosges plants. Free factory tours and tastings are offered.
new.tip: Listings give daily tours at about 10:00-11:30 and 14:00-18:00; confirm first. Address given is 680 route d'Épinal.
new.q: Confiserie Géromoise, 680 route d'Épinal, Gérardmer

new.title: Dine at La Table de Julie in Pont-à-Mousson
new.desc: A newer restaurant on Place Duroc serving French gastronomic and terroir cooking, with an expected budget of about 35 to 45 euros a meal. The regional tourism office lists it among its restaurants.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner; the old arcaded square is a pleasant setting.
new.q: La Table de Julie, 64 place Duroc, Pont-à-Mousson

new.title: Eat at Le Floréal near Lunéville château
new.desc: A restaurant on Place Léopold, two minutes from the château, run for over 20 years by two brothers. Gault&Millau gives it 11/20 with a budget of 23 to 44 euros a head excluding drinks.
new.tip: A handy lunch stop after the château. Check opening days locally.
new.q: Le Floréal, 1 Place Léopold, Lunéville

new.title: Buy chocolates at Pâtisserie Jean-Luc in Remiremont
new.desc: A pâtisserie-chocolaterie on rue Charles-de-Gaulle, founded in 1970, which a Petit Futé entry lists among the town's gourmet addresses. It is also listed among Remiremont wedding-cake suppliers.
new.tip: Rue Charles-de-Gaulle is lined with 18th-century arcades, so combine it with the abbey quarter.
new.q: Pâtisserie Jean Luc, 114 rue Charles de Gaulle, Remiremont

new.title: Try the tasting menu at Logan Laug in Saint-Dié
new.desc: A modern restaurant at 7 rue du 11-Novembre-1918. Gault&Millau describes French gastronomic and local cooking with evening tasting menus from 53 to 90 euros, and Michelin lists it at the three-euro-sign level.
new.tip: Book for evening menus; local chanterelles and ceps feature in season.
new.q: Logan Laug, 7 rue du 11 Novembre 1918, Saint-Dié-des-Vosges

new.title: Order tourte au munster at Le Rétro in Vittel
new.desc: A restaurant in the spa town of Vittel that lists a tourte au munster des Vosges among its specialities, according to the Tables & Auberges guide.
new.tip: I could not verify current hours or address from the listing; check before you go.
new.q: Restaurant Le Rétro, Vittel

new.title: Lunch at Baccarat Café in the crystal town
new.desc: A brasserie and tavern at 13 rue du Port in Baccarat, run in connection with the crystal house, listed by the Meurthe-et-Moselle tourism office.
new.tip: Reservations by phone or email per its listing; pair it with the crystal museum.
new.q: Baccarat Café, 13 rue du Port, Baccarat

new.title: Dine at Les Ducs de Lorraine in Épinal
new.desc: The most prominent fine-dining address in Épinal, rated 14.5 out of 20 by Gault&Millau and in modern French style.
new.tip: The Michelin status listed on one page could not be confirmed; check the restaurant's own site and book ahead.
new.q: Les Ducs de Lorraine, Épinal

new.title: Hike to the Grande Cascade de Tendon
new.desc: The great waterfall, about 32 metres high, is called the largest in the Vosges. A loop of about 6.3 to 6.5 km with some 230-250 metres of climb takes in the Grande and Petite cascades near Le Tholy.
new.tip: Park at the Col de Bonne Fontaine; the descent to the small waterfall is steep, so wear proper shoes.
new.q: Grande Cascade de Tendon, route de Tendon, Le Tholy

new.title: Walk around the Lac de Longemer
new.desc: A marked path of about 5 km circles the glacial lake at about 736 metres, taking one to one and a half hours. Swimming is unsupervised in places and forbidden along the road sides.
new.tip: Check signage before swimming. The neighbouring Lac de Retournemer is closed to bathing.
new.q: Lac de Longemer, Xonrupt-Longemer

new.title: Cruise or pedal across the Lac de Gérardmer
new.desc: Commented lake tours of 20 to 30 minutes run on boats such as L'Étoile and La Mouette from Easter to All Saints. Pedal boats and electric boats can be hired from April to mid-October.
new.tip: Operators run weather permitting; the lakeside path is also about 5 to 6 km on foot.
new.q: Lac de Gérardmer, Gérardmer

new.title: Walk to the Saut des Cuves waterfall
new.desc: A waterfall on the Vologne between Gérardmer and Xonrupt-Longemer, winding between granite blocks in a small gorge. Several trails start there, including the sentier des perles de la Vologne.
new.tip: Rocks are slippery when wet. A trail page notes the Saut de la Bourrique was closed from March 2024, so check access.
new.q: Saut des Cuves, Xonrupt-Longemer

new.title: Ride the all-season luge at La Bresse Hohneck
new.desc: The La Bresse Hohneck ski area, the largest in north-east France, has a four-season rail luge called Schlitte Mountain plus a children's luge. La Bresse Lispach also has a luge track.
new.tip: Summer opening details were not found, so check labresse.net before visiting.
new.q: Schlitte Mountain, 88 route de Vologne, La Bresse Hohneck, La Bresse

new.title: Cycle the Voie Bleue from Pont-à-Mousson to Nancy
new.desc: A stage of about 35 km of the Moselle-Saône cycle route follows the Moselle and Meurthe confluence to Nancy, taking roughly two hours twenty. It starts near the abbey and passes the wide lock at Blénod.
new.tip: Some Voie Bleue signs may be missing around Pont-à-Mousson, so carry the stage map from lavoiebleue.com.
new.q: Abbaye des Prémontrés, Pont-à-Mousson

new.title: Attend the Gérardmer fantasy film festival
new.desc: The Festival international du film fantastique de Gérardmer has run each year since 1994, towards the end of January. The 2026 edition was held 27 January to 1 February.
new.tip: Check festival-gerardmer.com for 2027 dates and ticketing.
new.q: Espace Lac, Gérardmer

new.title: Watch Vosges linen woven at Garnier-Thiebaut
new.desc: The Gérardmer linen maker weaves household linen using the Jacquard technique at its Kichompré factory, which also has a shop on site. Free tours exist, by registration only.
new.tip: Register by email to the company; the most recent dates found were in 2025, so ask for the current schedule.
new.q: Garnier-Thiebaut, 11 boulevard de Granges, Kichompré, Gérardmer

new.title: Explore the medieval town of Liverdun
new.desc: Liverdun's old town sits above a loop of the Moselle a few kilometres from Nancy. The Porte Haute is framed by a square tower and a round one, and the Moselle valley and Liverdun west part form a site inscrit since 1967.
new.tip: Follow the tourist circuit of the haute ville; the Garenne park with the Art Nouveau château Corbin is nearby.
new.q: Porte Haute, Liverdun

new.title: Walk Toul's Vauban ramparts from the Porte de Metz
new.desc: Toul's ramparts were built between 1700 and 1722 to Vauban's design, with nine bastions and three gates, and are part of the 2008 UNESCO listing. Porte de Metz is the only gate keeping Vauban's original drawbridge.
new.tip: A free route leaflet is available at the Maison du Tourisme des Terres Touloises; the circuit takes about 45 minutes.
new.q: Porte de Metz, Toul

new.title: Swim at the Lac de Bouzey
new.desc: A lake at Sanchey near Épinal with two laid-out beaches, supervised summer bathing in the afternoons, pedal-boat hire and a walking circuit. Hours vary by source.
new.tip: Bathing is supervised July and August afternoons only according to listings; check locally.
new.q: Lac de Bouzey, Sanchey

new.title: Browse the Village de Saint-Nicolas market in Épinal
new.desc: Épinal's Christmas market is set up around the Basilique Saint-Maurice with more than forty wooden chalets. The 2026 season runs from 27 November to 1 January with the parade of floats on 5 December.
new.tip: Entry is free. Parking is available in the centre and the station is a ten-minute walk.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Maurice, Place des Vosges, Épinal

new.title: Hike up the Saint-Mont above Remiremont
new.desc: The Saint-Mont is a viewpoint hill tied to the Saint-Romaric and Saint-Amé double monastery, reached only on foot. A loop of about 6.9 km reaches about 664 metres and passes the chapel of Vieux Saint-Amé.
new.tip: Park at Saint-Étienne-lès-Remiremont; the climb is steep and stony in places.
new.q: Saint-Mont, Saint-Étienne-lès-Remiremont

new.title: Hike the Hohneck from Lac de Retournemer
new.desc: The Hohneck rises to 1,363 metres with a 360 degree panorama over the Alsace plain, and a hike starts from the Lac de Retournemer on the Lorraine side. A path links the Route des Crêtes to the summit road.
new.tip: Weather can change fast on the ridge. Retournemer itself is closed to swimming.
new.q: Lac de Retournemer, Xonrupt-Longemer
